Hi Karthik / Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the MSA. Attached are our standard redlines — we highlighted two items we need a decision on this week: choice of law and emergency relief for preservation/injunctions. High level: AcmeCloud generally pushes for Delaware law and exclusive state court for injunctive relief in CA for customer data preservation (we have a lot of CA-based subsidiaries). We know Redwood prefers a single forum.

Specific asks:
- Can Redwood accept Delaware as governing law? If not, do you accept a compromise where the MSA is governed by Delaware but AcmeCloud can seek provisional injunctive relief in California courts to preserve evidence or stop immediate harm?
- We also ask for an explicit interim access/preservation clause so our security team can comply quickly with subpoenas/local regulator requests.

Attached: ACM-Redlines-Nov15.docx (redlines + comments).

We have procurement timelines next Wednesday — can we get a position by end of day Tuesday? Happy to hop on a 20-min call if useful.

Thanks,
Marie Tan
Senior Contracts Manager | AcmeCloud

Subject: Re: AcmeCloud MSA redlines — governing law & interim relief

Marie — thanks for the redlines and the clarity on timelines.

Short answer: Redwood wants a single, predictable governing law and forum for operational reasons (support, liability frameworks, and consistency with our hosting agreements). That said, we understand the need for quick preservation remedies for customer data.

Proposed compromise (prelim):
- Governing law: Delaware (state) — main MSA.
- Dispute resolution: Binding arbitration for all non-emergency disputes (subject to caps).
- Carveout for emergency equitable relief: Either party may seek provisional injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to preserve the status quo, obtain evidence preservation, or prevent immediate irreparable harm. If the party seeking relief is AcmeCloud and files in CA, Redwood will accept the temporary jurisdiction for the injunctive action only and will not assert forum non conveniens for that narrow relief.
- Process: 48-hour notice to the other party + expedited meet/call with legal ops before filing where feasible; formal arbitration to follow for the underlying claim.

Kimberly / Rishi — can you confirm if legal can live with the above carveout as written? If yes, I'll send a redline for Marie and Acme to review.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Karthik / all — captured and thanks for the suggested compromise. My read: acceptable with a few clarifications to limit risk. Draft notes below — I'll attach a short text file with proposed language.

Key legal points:
- Agree to Delaware governing law for the substantive MSA.
- Emergency carveout is OK but must be explicitly limited to "provisional equitable relief necessary to preserve the status quo or prevent imminent and irreparable harm" — we should exclude routine discovery disputes or contract interpretation arguments.
- Require that any temporary injunctive relief obtained is limited in scope and duration and that the party seeking relief must promptly (within 7 days) refer the matter to arbitration for final determination.
- For CA filings specifically: Redwood will not contest jurisdiction for provisional relief only, provided AcmeCloud confirms in writing that the relief sought is narrowly tailored (security/preservation) and provides immediate notice to Redwood legal-ops.
- Add a mutual confidentiality carve for any emergency briefing materials.

I'll attach 'redwood-proposed-emergency-clause.txt' with markup. If AcmeCloud accepts, we should be ready to push the MSA to sign pending exec sign-off on any material concessions (we should flag to finance/legal for the small risk window).

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Subject: Re: AcmeCloud MSA redlines — governing law & interim relief

Kimberly — appreciate the thought-through response and the limited language. We can accept the carveout as proposed with two small tweaks:

1) If provisional injunctive relief is sought in CA, AcmeCloud requests that Redwood agrees not to remove the action to arbitration (i.e., do not compel arbitration of the provisional relief filing) until after the emergency order is issued and the underlying arbitration is initiated. We want to avoid delay in preservation steps.
2) If the party obtains a provisional order, the parties will cooperate to agree on an expedited schedule for arbitration on the underlying dispute; failing agreement, the party seeking relief can set the initial schedule and the arbitrator will be asked to adopt an expedited procedure.

If you can confirm those two points in writing, procurement will proceed to finalize and we can get a DocuSign out. Willing to sign-off on exec approval for the narrow carveout.

Best,
Marie

Marie — thanks. Kimberly and I reviewed and we can confirm both points. To restate for the record (so procurement has a single bullet):

- Governing law: Delaware.
- All substantive disputes: binding arbitration (per MSA).
- Limited carveout: either party may seek provisional equitable relief (to preserve status quo, prevent immediate irreparable harm, or preservation of evidence) in any court of competent jurisdiction; if filed in CA by AcmeCloud, Redwood will not move to compel arbitration to vacate or stay the provisional relief prior to issuance of the temporary order.
- If provisional relief is entered, parties will promptly confer and either agree to an expedited arbitration schedule or the claimant may set an initial expedited schedule (arbitrator to adopt if necessary).
- Parties will provide at least 48 hours' good-faith notice to the other party's legal-ops before filing, unless notice would cause irreparable harm.

I'll circulate a final one-page summary and updated redline to your DocuSign link by EOD so procurement can complete. Thanks for the quick coordination.

Karthik
